newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares end stronger, focus on C.Amorim.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares end stronger, focus on C.Amorim.

text.p: Portuguese shares closed higher in line with European markets, but off the session's highs, after the market drew breath from the Fed's decision not to raise interest rates, for now at least. The most active stocks included cement group Cimpor, Banco Comercial Portugues, Portucel Industrial and retailer Sonae Investimentos, which hit a high for the year. Cork group Corticeira Amorim hit a low for the year of 1,470 escudos as investors were disappointed with the recent performance of the company, dealers said. "Most investors are disillusioned with the company's performance, as it has shown results far short of expectations in recent years," said one. Another said: "The first quarter results could be another disappointment."

* Dealers said buying on Lisbon bourse was limited because investors were raising cash to invest in the privatisation of state utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal. They said optimism could return to the market in force after the sell-off of EDP shares on June 16.
